question: If the diagonals of a rhombus are 10 cm and 24 cm, then what is the perimeter of the rhombus?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The side of a rhombus is the hypotenuse of a right triangle formed by half of its diagonals.

Side = √((d₁ ÷ 2)² + (d₂ ÷ 2)²)

⇒ Side = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 cm

Perimeter = 4 × Side = 4 × 13 = 52 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first diagonal (AC) = 24 cm

Length of second diagonal (BD) = 10 cm

**Formula Used:**

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles (90°).

By Pythagoras theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Perimeter of a rhombus = 4 × side

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/906a57d5508fcceb8742c10902feb956681acd374d795c10645d487ad944784f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Half of diagonal AC (OA) = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Half of diagonal BD (OB) = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ In right-angled ΔAOB, the intersection at center O forms a 90° angle.

⇒ Applying Pythagoras theorem in ΔAOB:

⇒ AB² = OA² + OB²

⇒ a² = 12² + 5²

⇒ a² = 144 + 25

⇒ a² = 169

⇒ a = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ The perimeter of the rhombus = 4 × a

⇒ Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 52 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for Perimeter

The perimeter of a rhombus can be calculated directly from its diagonals using the formula: P = 2 × √(d₁² + d₂²).

Area of Rhombus

The area of a rhombus is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂.

Properties of Rhombus

All four sides of a rhombus are equal in length, and opposite sides are parallel. Its diagonals bisect interior angles and are perpendicular bisectors of each other.
